chunks: Third: It is to say that according to you, the benefit of the Imamate is that it leads away from the ugly (wrong). However, this is not achieved with his existence being in hiding, so his existence does not differ from his non-existence. And if his hidden existence does not possess the mode of necessity they mentioned, your evidence does not necessitate his existence during the occultation. Therefore, your evidence, even though it is invalidated where the hand is extended (administration), and extending the hand was not necessitated during the occultation, is not related to the existence of an Imam who does not extend his hand, nor is it achieved in this state.

key_terms.الْإِمَامَةِ: Imamate (the institution of religious and political leadership)
key_terms.الْغَيْبَةِ: Occultation (the state of being hidden from public view)
key_terms.انْبِسَاطِ الْيَدِ: Extending the hand (metaphor for active administration and authority)

ai.seo_question: What is the theological objection to the necessity of the Imam during the occultation?
ai.summary: This passage from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* addresses the Mu'tazili objection that the Imam’s primary function—preventing moral corruption through active governance (*mub'ad min al-qubh*)—is nullified during the occultation, rendering his presence indistinguishable from absence. Tusi counters that the Imam’s existence retains its obligatory necessity regardless of his physical visibility, as the proof for his Imamate is not contingent upon the continuous manifestation of administrative power. This establishes the theological foundation for the validity of the Hidden Imam’s authority even when he is not actively 'extending his hand' to enforce justice.
